structure.caption: Figure 4: Q1 2026 Customer Experience Performance Summary

spec.title: Q1 2026 Customer Experience Performance Summary
spec.subtitle: Ref: CX-1457357 | Date: 12 April 2026 | From: Elena Marquez, VP Customer Experience

sections.heading: Executive Overview
sections.body: Q1 2026 results confirm that reducing effort in high-friction digital journeys is the most direct path to improving customer advocacy. Overall NPS increased modestly from 18 in Q4 2025 to 22, while CSAT rose from 78% to 81%. However, customers who reported low-effort digital experiences scored 41 NPS on average, compared to -12 among those who struggled with account access or billing. Contact volume increased 6% year-over-year, largely driven by repeat contacts tied to unresolved digital issues.

sections.heading: Channel Performance Snapshot
sections.body: By channel, Mobile App NPS improved to 28 (up 5 points), while Web Portal NPS remained flat at 15 due to login and password reset failures. Contact Center CSAT held steady at 83%, though average handle time increased by 42 seconds because agents were assisting with digital navigation issues. Chat support posted the highest CSAT at 87% but also the highest reported effort score (3.4 out of 5), reflecting multiple handoffs. In-branch interactions, though limited in volume, achieved the strongest NPS at 36.

sections.heading: Verbatim Sentiment Themes
sections.body: Analysis of 3,842 open-text responses highlighted recurring themes: difficulty accessing accounts after security updates, confusion around prorated billing charges, and inconsistent error messaging in the app. Positive feedback centered on knowledgeable phone agents and faster dispute resolution once connected. Negative comments frequently referenced needing to "try three times to log in" and "not understanding the new statement layout." Customers experiencing billing confusion were 2.3x more likely to become detractors.

sections.heading: Journey Pain Points
sections.body: The account access journey recorded the highest effort score at 3.8, primarily due to multi-factor authentication timeouts and unclear password requirements. The billing review and payment journey showed a CSAT of 74%, the lowest of all measured journeys, with 18% of users abandoning before completing payment. Customers who failed digital payment were 40% more likely to call within 24 hours, directly contributing to increased contact center load. Resolving these two journeys is projected to reduce inbound calls by up to 9%.

sections.heading: Customer Improvement Action Plan
sections.body: Immediate actions for Q2 include simplifying password reset flows, introducing real-time billing explanations within statements, and deploying proactive in-app alerts before payment due dates. A cross-functional task force between Digital, Billing Operations, and IT has been established with a 90-day target to reduce digital effort scores below 3.0. Additionally, we will implement closed-loop follow-up for detractors within 48 hours to recover at-risk relationships. Success will be measured by a target NPS of 28 and CSAT of 84% by the end of Q2 2026.

structure.full_text:
Q1 2026 Customer Experience Performance Summary
Ref: CX-1457357 | Date: 12 April 2026 | From: Elena Marquez, VP Customer Experience

Section Executive Overview
Q1 2026 results confirm that reducing effort in high-friction digital journeys is the most direct path to improving customer advocacy. Overall NPS increased modestly from 18 in Q4 2025 to 22, while CSAT rose from 78% to 81%. However, customers who reported low-effort digital experiences scored 41 NPS on average, compared to -12 among those who struggled with account access or billing. Contact volume increased 6% year-over-year, largely driven by repeat contacts tied to unresolved digital issues.

Section Channel Performance Snapshot
By channel, Mobile App NPS improved to 28 (up 5 points), while Web Portal NPS remained flat at 15 due to login and password reset failures. Contact Center CSAT held steady at 83%, though average handle time increased by 42 seconds because agents were assisting with digital navigation issues. Chat support posted the highest CSAT at 87% but also the highest reported effort score (3.4 out of 5), reflecting multiple handoffs. In-branch interactions, though limited in volume, achieved the strongest NPS at 36.

Section Verbatim Sentiment Themes
Analysis of 3,842 open-text responses highlighted recurring themes: difficulty accessing accounts after security updates, confusion around prorated billing charges, and inconsistent error messaging in the app. Positive feedback centered on knowledgeable phone agents and faster dispute resolution once connected. Negative comments frequently referenced needing to "try three times to log in" and "not understanding the new statement layout." Customers experiencing billing confusion were 2.3x more likely to become detractors.

Section Journey Pain Points
The account access journey recorded the highest effort score at 3.8, primarily due to multi-factor authentication timeouts and unclear password requirements. The billing review and payment journey showed a CSAT of 74%, the lowest of all measured journeys, with 18% of users abandoning before completing payment. Customers who failed digital payment were 40% more likely to call within 24 hours, directly contributing to increased contact center load. Resolving these two journeys is projected to reduce inbound calls by up to 9%.

Section Customer Improvement Action Plan
Immediate actions for Q2 include simplifying password reset flows, introducing real-time billing explanations within statements, and deploying proactive in-app alerts before payment due dates. A cross-functional task force between Digital, Billing Operations, and IT has been established with a 90-day target to reduce digital effort scores below 3.0. Additionally, we will implement closed-loop follow-up for detractors within 48 hours to recover at-risk relationships. Success will be measured by a target NPS of 28 and CSAT of 84% by the end of Q2 2026.

Confidential — Internal Distribution Only | Page 1 of 1
